# nish/net/http1-server

The server side of HTTP/1.1 (RFC 9112): a sans-IO connection that drives `nish/net/http1-codec`'s parser, and two pools of them for a program that owns its readiness loop, one on `nish:net`'s plain TCP and one on `nish/net/tls-tcp` with ALPN `http/1.1`.

```ts
import {
  H1_AGAIN,
  H1_ALPN,
  H1_BODY,
  H1_CLOSED,
  H1_DONE,
  H1_END,
  H1_ERROR,
  H1_INVALID,
  H1_NEED_MORE,
  H1_POOL_FULL,
  H1_REQUEST,
  H1_WANT_READ,
  H1_WANT_WRITE,
  H1_WRITE,
  H1_WS_CLOSE,
  H1_WS_MESSAGE,
  Http1Config,
  Http1Connection,
  Http1OutputPool,
  Http1Server,
  Http1TlsServer,
  HttpDate,
} from "nish/net/http1-server";
```

<scalar-code-group>

```ts example.ts
const listener = tcpListen("0.0.0.0", 8080, 128);
const server = new Http1Server(new Http1Config(), listener, 64);
// when the listener is readable:
const slot: i32 = server.accept();
if (slot >= 0) { pollAdd(loop, server.fd(slot), 1, slot); }
// when a connection's token comes back:
let wants: i32 = (events & 5) !== 0 ? server.readable(slot) : server.writable(slot);
let event: i32 = server.next(slot);
while (event !== H1_NEED_MORE && event !== H1_ERROR) {
  const conn: Http1Connection = server.connection(slot);
  // H1_REQUEST: conn.parser.methodIs("GET"), conn.parser.targetIs("/"), ...
  //   conn.respond(200, names, values, HTTP1_CHUNKED)
  // H1_BODY: conn.data[conn.dataStart .. conn.dataStart + conn.dataLength)
  // H1_END: conn.write(body, 0, n); conn.end()
  event = server.next(slot);
}
wants = server.flush(slot);
if ((wants & H1_DONE) !== 0) { server.close(slot); }
else if (server.rearm(slot, wants)) { pollModify(loop, server.fd(slot), wants & 3, slot); }
```

</scalar-code-group>

<scalar-detail title="Events">

`next()` answers `H1_REQUEST` (a request's head: the parser's
spans and `...Is` methods read it), `H1_BODY` (some of its body, de-chunked,
a window that stays valid until the next `next()`), `H1_END` (the request
is complete), `H1_WRITE` (a write that was held back may be tried again),
`H1_WS_MESSAGE` and `H1_WS_CLOSE` once the slot has switched to WebSocket,
and `H1_ERROR`, final: the request broke a rule, the response that says so
is queued, and the connection closes once it is sent. `H1_NEED_MORE` asks
for more input, for the output to drain, or for the program to finish the
response it owes.

</scalar-detail>

<scalar-detail title="One exchange at a time">

A request is answered before the next one on
the connection is read: `respond`, any number of `write`s, `end`. A
response with a length is over once its last byte is written, and one with
no body (`Content-Length: 0`, HEAD, 204, 304) once its head is, so `end` is
optional for both; a chunked body, and an unframed one to HTTP/1.0, has no
length to count and is over only at `end`, without which the connection
waits and the next request is never answered. The program may answer at
once (before the body has arrived) or after `H1_END`; either way the
request's body is read to its end before the next request starts, which is
what keeps pipelined requests in order (§9.3.2).
Pipelined bytes wait in the parser's buffer, and once it holds
`inputLimit()` bytes the connection stops asking for input, so the client's
TCP window closes: back-pressure on the way in.

</scalar-detail>

<scalar-detail title="Streaming both ways">

A request body arrives a chunk at a time, at most
`chunkSize` bytes in each `H1_BODY`, whether it was sent with
`Content-Length` or chunked. A response is written with a length or chunked,
a `write` at a time into the output buffer; a `write` takes what fits and
answers how much, and when it could not take everything the connection
answers `H1_NEED_MORE` until the socket has drained half the output, then
`H1_WRITE`. Until then it reads nothing, so the window the program is writing
from stays valid: back-pressure on the way out.

Nothing buffers a whole body. On an `Http1Server` slot `sendBody` sends a
body with a length from the program's own array, the queued output with it,
and copies only what the socket did not take, under the same rules.

</scalar-detail>

<scalar-detail title="What the server decides">

The framing field (`Content-Length` or
`Transfer-Encoding: chunked`) and the `Connection` field are the server's;
the program's fields may not hold either, nor `Upgrade`, `Keep-Alive` or
`Content-Length`. A request that did not ask to keep the connection open
gets `Connection: close` and the connection closes after it; an HTTP/1.0
request that asked for keep-alive gets `Connection: keep-alive`; a chunked
response to an HTTP/1.0 request is sent unframed and ends with the
connection, since chunked is HTTP/1.1's. A response to HEAD, and a 204 or
304, carries no body whatever the program writes (RFC 9110 §9.3.2, §15.3.5,
§15.4.5). A 1xx before the final response (100 Continue) is allowed; 101 is
`acceptWebSocket`'s.

</scalar-detail>

<scalar-detail title="The Date">

Every final response, an error included, carries a `Date`
field (RFC 9110 §6.6.1) from `HttpDate`, which formats the IMF-fixdate at
most once a second; a 1xx carries none. The pool's slots share one, so a
busy server formats a second once, not once a slot. A program that sets its
own `date` field sends that one instead, so a response has one `Date`.
`Http1Server` reads the clock once per serve call — from `readable` or
`writable` to the `flush` that ends it — and every response written in
between carries that reading; one written outside a serve call, an answer
given later, reads the clock then. `date.pin(unixMs)` fixes it, for a test
that compares bytes.

</scalar-detail>

<scalar-callout type="warning">

**Refusals.** Every refusal of `nish/net/http1-codec`'s parser — the smuggling
shapes, a `Content-Length` with a `Transfer-Encoding`, two that disagree,
a malformed chunk size — is answered with its status (400, 413, 414, 431,
501, 505), `Content-Length: 0` and `Connection: close`, and ends the
connection; so does a malformed WebSocket frame, with its close code.
`docs/security/http1-codec.md` is the record.

</scalar-callout>

<scalar-detail title="WebSocket">

A request that asked to upgrade reaches the program like any
other; `acceptWebSocket(protocol)` answers it with the 101 of
`nish/net/websocket` when it is a valid opening handshake (RFC 6455 §4.2),
and once its exchange is over the slot reads frames with a `WsDecoder`
instead of requests, the bytes that followed the request included. A ping
is answered with a pong and a close with a close, by the connection.

</scalar-detail>

<scalar-callout type="warning">

**Caps are start-up numbers**, all in `Http1Config`: the request target, the
header section and its field count, a request body, the chunk handed over,
the output buffer, a WebSocket message, the idle timeout and the deadline for
a whole request head (`headTimeout`, against slowloris); the slots are the
pool's size.

`Http1Server` builds a slot's connection on the first accept into it and
keeps it, so a pool sized for its peak costs at start-up only what does not
depend on the size, and holds at most `size` connections once the peak has
come; `Http1TlsServer` does the same for a slot's connection and, through
`TlsTcpServer`, its TLS state. Every buffer is allocated with its slot or
grown to its cap on first use and kept, so a warmed slot serves request after
request with `Arena.used()` flat. Accepting a WebSocket allocates (the accept
key), once a connection.

</scalar-callout>

<scalar-detail title="Output is borrowed">

The pools' slots share an `Http1OutputPool`: a
connection takes an `outputSize` buffer when it first needs room to write
and gives it back once its carrier has sent everything, so the output
memory a pool holds follows the connections the socket is holding back,
not its size. A pool that ever had `n` connections writing at once keeps
`n` buffers and allocates no more.

</scalar-detail>

Private helpers share the importing program's flat symbol namespace
(`docs/wp26-stdlib.md` §3e), which is why each one carries the module's name.

Written from RFC 9112, RFC 9110 and RFC 6455, not ported from another
implementation.

## Classes

### Http1Config

The caps of every connection made from it, fixed when the connection is
made. Each is a number the program sets once, at start-up.

```ts
class Http1Config
```

| Member | |
| --- | --- |
| `new Http1Config()` |  |
| `chunkSize: i32` | The most body bytes one `H1_BODY` hands over, and how much is read from the socket at once. |
| `headTimeout: i32` | Milliseconds a request head may take, from its first byte to its blank line, before `expire` closes the slot however steadily its bytes come. The idle timeout alone restarts on every byte, so a client that sends one byte of its head each `idleTimeout` would hold its slot for good (slowloris). |
| `idleInput: boolean` | Lend a slot's input and head buffers back to the server between exchanges: once a response is sent and no byte of the next request has come, the slot gives both to pools the server's slots share, and takes them again with the next byte. The memory they hold then follows the connections mid-request rather than every keep-alive connection open, for two pool operations a request. Off by default. |
| `idleTimeout: i32` | Milliseconds without a byte read or written after which `expire` closes a slot. |
| `lingerBytes: i32` | The most bytes a refused slot drains before it is closed whatever is left (RFC 9112 §9.6); 0 closes at once, without a lingering close. |
| `lingerTimeout: i32` | Milliseconds `Http1Server` keeps reading, and throwing away, what a refused client still sends after its error response, before `expire` closes the slot (RFC 9112 §9.6). The server shuts its write side and drains rather than closing at once: a close with unread bytes resets the connection, and the reset can destroy the response before the client reads it. |
| `maxBody: i32` | The longest request body, declared or de-chunked; past it, 413. |
| `maxHeaderBytes: i32` | The longest header section, and trailer section; past it, 431. |
| `maxHeaders: i32` | The most fields in a header section, trailers counted; past it, 431. |
| `maxMessage: i32` | The longest WebSocket message, its fragments together; past it, close 1009. At most 2^30 − 14, so a whole frame fits the decoder's input. |
| `maxTarget: i32` | The longest request target; past it, 414. With `maxHeaderBytes`, at most 2^30 − 44, the most a head buffer holds. |
| `outputSize: i32` | The output buffer, in bytes: the most of a response waiting for the socket. |

### Http1Connection

One connection's HTTP/1.1 server, sans-IO: bytes in through `feed`, events
out of `next`, and the response the program writes in
`output[outputStart .. outputEnd)` for its carrier to send.

```ts
class Http1Connection
```

| Member | |
| --- | --- |
| `new Http1Connection(config: Http1Config)` | A connection under `config`. A cap outside what the connection can work with panics. |
| `bufferLimit: i32` | The most input the connection buffers, unread: the cap `inputRoom` holds it to. |
| `closeAfter: boolean` | The connection closes once this exchange is over. |
| `data: u8[]` | `H1_BODY`'s and `H1_WS_MESSAGE`'s bytes. |
| `dataLength: i32` | How many bytes `H1_BODY` or `H1_WS_MESSAGE` handed over, from `data[dataStart]`. |
| `dataStart: i32` | Where the bytes `H1_BODY` or `H1_WS_MESSAGE` handed over start in `data`. |
| `date: HttpDate` | The `Date` every final response carries. The connection makes its own; `Http1Server` and `Http1TlsServer` put theirs here, so that every slot of a pool shares one and the pool formats at most once a second. A program may put another, to share it or to pin its clock. |
| `fd: i32` | The plain TCP socket the carrier sends `output` on, which `sendBody` writes to directly: `Http1Server.accept` sets it, and `restart` and `abort` put it back to -1. -1 for a connection with no such socket (a sans-IO carrier, `Http1TlsServer`'s TLS records), where `sendBody` copies as `write` does. |
| `heads: Http1OutputPool \| null` | Where the parser's head buffer goes while the slot rests, beside `inputs`; null otherwise. |
| `headSince: i64` | When the head being read began to arrive, in `monotonicNanos`; meaningful while `headTimed`. |
| `headTimed: boolean` | A head has begun to arrive and is not read whole yet: `headSince` is its deadline's start. |
| `inputs: Http1OutputPool \| null` | Where the parser's input and head buffers go while the slot rests, with `Http1Config.idleInput`; null otherwise. |
| `lastActive: i64` | When the carrier last moved a byte for the connection, in `monotonicNanos`. |
| `lingerSince: i64` | When the lingering close began, in `monotonicNanos`; meaningful while `lingering`. |
| `mss: i32` | The TCP maximum segment size the program sets for this connection, for `respondEncoded` under `HttpCompressor.segmentMode`; 0, the default, leaves it to the compressor and the socket (`segmentMss`). Each accept puts it back to 0. |
| `noOutput: u8[]` | The empty array `output` is while the connection holds no buffer. |
| `opcode: i32` | `H1_WS_MESSAGE`'s opcode: text or binary. |
| `output: u8[]` | Bytes to send are `output[outputStart .. outputEnd)`. Empty until the connection first needs room to write: then its own buffer, made once, or one borrowed from `pool` and given back by `release` once sent. |
| `outputEnd: i32` | Where the unsent bytes end in `output`, one past the last; equal to `outputStart` when nothing waits. |
| `outputStart: i32` | Where the unsent bytes start in `output`; a carrier sends from here and calls `consume` with what it sent. |
| `parser: Http1Parser` | The request parser: its head (`methodIs`, `targetIs`, `header`, spans) is the current request's from its `H1_REQUEST` until its response is done, `H1_END` included, however much of a pipelined request is fed behind it. |
| `pong: u8[]` | A ping's payload, kept until its pong fits: empty until the first ping. |
| `pool: Http1OutputPool \| null` | Where `output` is borrowed from, for a connection of a pool; null for one that keeps its own. |
| `responseEmpty: boolean` | The response carries no body (HEAD, 204, 304): what is written is dropped. |
| `socketMss: i32` | The MSS `Http1Server.accept` read from this connection's socket (`netMss`), or 0 when it reports none. |
| `status: i32` | `H1_ERROR`'s HTTP status or WebSocket close code, or `H1_WS_CLOSE`'s close code. |
| `writeHeld: boolean` | A write was held back; `next` answers nothing but `H1_WRITE` until there is room. |
| `ws: WsDecoder \| null` | The frame decoder: made when the slot first switches to WebSocket, so a slot that only ever speaks HTTP never holds its buffers, then kept for the slot's later peers. |
| `abort(): void` | The socket failed: nothing more is sent or read, and the connection is done. |
| `acceptEncoding(): i32` | The content coding to answer the current request with, read from its `Accept-Encoding` with gzip offered (`httpAcceptEncoding`): `HTTP_CODING_GZIP`, `HTTP_CODING_IDENTITY` (also with no such field), or `HTTP_CODING_NONE` when the client refuses identity and does not take gzip. Allocates nothing. Read at `H1_REQUEST`, `H1_BODY` or `H1_END` alike: the head stays the request's until its response is done. |
| `acceptWebSocket(protocol: string): i32` | Accepts the current request's WebSocket opening handshake (RFC 6455 §4.2.2) with `protocol`, empty for none: the 101 is queued, and once the request has ended the slot reads frames. Answers 0; `H1_INVALID` when the request is not a valid opening handshake (the program answers 400, or 426 for the wrong version) or `protocol` is not a token; `H1_AGAIN` when the output has no room yet; `H1_CLOSED` with no request to answer. |
| `answerable(): boolean` | Whether the program may answer the current request now. |
| `closeWebSocket(code: i32): i32` | Starts the closing handshake (§5.5.1, §7.1.2) with `code`: a close frame, then the connection is done once it is sent. Answers 0, `H1_INVALID` for a code that may not be sent, or `H1_CLOSED` when the slot is not an open WebSocket. |
| `consume(n: i32): void` | Marks the first `n` bytes of the output sent. |
| `end(): i32` | Ends the response: the last chunk of a chunked body. Answers 0; `H1_INVALID` for a response with a length that still owes bytes; `H1_AGAIN` when the last chunk does not fit yet; `H1_CLOSED` with no response under way.<br><br>Required for a chunked body, and for an unframed one (a chunked response to HTTP/1.0), which only `end` can say is over: without it the connection waits and the next request is never read. Optional for a response with no body or a `Content-Length` written in full, which the connection finishes itself when it moves to the next request; called before then it answers 0, and after then `H1_CLOSED`. |
| `ended(): boolean` | Whether the peer's byte stream has ended (`endInput`): a request still held on the connection is one its client hung up on, or half-closed. |
| `endInput(): void` | The peer's byte stream has ended: once what it sent is answered, the connection is done. |
| `feed(buf: u8[], off: i32, len: i32): i32` | Takes as much of `buf[off .. off + len)` as `inputRoom` allows and answers how much; the rest is the caller's to feed again later. A window outside `buf` panics. |
| `headArrived(now: i64): void` | Starts the head deadline at `now` (`monotonicNanos`) when bytes of a request head wait to be read and its clock has not started. The carriers call it after each `feed`; a program that feeds a connection itself calls it the same way. Bytes that wait while the previous exchange is still open start no clock: they count from when it is over (`nextRequest`). |
| `identityRefused(): boolean` | Whether the current request's `Accept-Encoding` refuses the body as it is (`httpIdentityRefused`); `respondEncoded` then gzips any body it can. |
| `inputLimit(): i32` | The most input the connection holds unread: what `inputRoom` counts against. |
| `inputRoom(): i32` | How many bytes `feed` would take now: none while a write is held back or once the connection is closing. |
| `isDone(): boolean` | Whether the connection is over and everything is sent: the carrier closes it. |
| `isWebSocket(): boolean` | Whether the slot has switched to WebSocket and is open. |
| `lingering(): boolean` | Whether the connection is in its lingering close: its refusal is sent and its carrier drains what the peer still sends. |
| `next(): i32` | The next event; see the module comment. |
| `park(): void` | Gives the parser's input and head buffers to `inputs` and `heads` while the connection rests between exchanges: speaking HTTP, no request open, nothing fed and unread. Does nothing without the pools or otherwise. |
| `release(): void` | Gives `output` back to the pool once nothing in it is waiting: no bytes to send, no write held back for room. The carrier calls it after each send; a connection that keeps its own buffer keeps it. |
| `respond(status: i32, names: u8[][], values: u8[][], bodyLength: i32): i32` | Answers the current request with `status` and the fields `names[k]`: `values[k]`, and the framing `bodyLength` asks for: a length, or `HTTP1_CHUNKED`, or `HTTP1_NO_BODY` for a 1xx, a 204 or a 304. A 1xx (but 101) is interim and the final status follows it. Answers 0; `H1_INVALID` for a status outside 100 to 599 or 101, a reserved field, a name or value `http1WriteResponseHead` refuses, or a head larger than the output; `H1_AGAIN` when the output has no room for it yet (`H1_WRITE` says when to try again); `H1_CLOSED` with no request to answer.<br><br>A response with no body (a `bodyLength` of 0, a HEAD, a 204 or a 304) is finished once this returns 0, and one with a length once `write` or `sendBody` has taken all of it: `end` is optional for both. A chunked body is finished only by `end`. |
| `respondEncoded(status: i32, names: u8[][], values: u8[][], body: u8[], off: i32, len: i32, enc: HttpCompressor, coding: i32): i32` | Answers the current request with all of `body[off .. off + len)` in one call: `respond`, `write` and `end`, the body compressed by `enc` when `coding` (from `acceptEncoding`) is gzip and `enc.compress` takes it, with `Content-Encoding: gzip` and the compressed `Content-Length`, and otherwise sent as it is; `Vary: Accept-Encoding` while `enc.vary` is set and the choice turned on the request (`HttpCompressor.varies`).<br><br>Under `enc.segmentMode` the compressed response goes out only when, head included, it takes fewer segments of `segmentMss(enc)` bytes than the body as it is, and a response that fits one segment as it is goes so without compressing (`enc.oneSegment`); `enc.decision` says what was chosen. A request that refuses identity (`identityRefused`) is sent gzip whatever the length, the saving or the segments (`enc.compressAnyway`). The program's fields may not name `Content-Encoding` or, with `enc.vary`, `Vary`.<br><br>The whole response is written or none of it: `H1_AGAIN` when the output has no room for it yet (`H1_WRITE` says when to try again, compressing again), `H1_INVALID` for a response larger than the output could ever hold or one `respond` refuses, `H1_CLOSED` with no request to answer; 0 once it is queued. A window outside `body` panics. |
| `restart(): void` | Puts the connection back as the constructor left it, for the next peer. It allocates nothing. |
| `segmentMss(enc: HttpCompressor): i32` | The segment `respondEncoded` counts in under `enc.segmentMode`: this connection's `mss` when the program set it, else `enc.mss` when the program set it (above 0), else the socket's (`socketMss`), else `HTTP_DEFAULT_MSS`. |
| `sendBody(buf: readonly u8[], off: i32, len: i32): i32` | `write` of `buf[off .. off + len)`, sent from `buf` itself where it can be: under a `Content-Length` response on a connection whose carrier named its socket (`fd`, set by `Http1Server.accept`) and with no write held back, the queued output and the body leave in one `netWrite2`, and only what the socket did not take is copied into the output, the way `write` copies it (what does not fit is answered short, and `H1_WRITE` says when to send the rest).<br><br>Once it returns the connection holds no reference to `buf`, so the caller may reuse or give back its bytes at once. A chunked or empty response, a write held back (`H1_AGAIN` or a short answer not yet followed by `H1_WRITE`), and a connection with no socket (`Http1TlsServer`, a sans-IO carrier) copy all of it: it is `write`, with the same bytes on the wire. Answers what `write` answers, `H1_INVALID` for more than the response still owes; `H1_CLOSED` also when the socket failed during the send, which aborts the connection. A window outside `buf` panics. As with `write`, a `Content-Length` body sent in full needs no `end`. |
| `sendFrame(fin: boolean, opcode: i32, buf: u8[], off: i32, len: i32): i32` | Sends one WebSocket frame, unmasked as a server's are (§5.1): a whole text or binary message, a fragment of one (`fin` false, then continuations), a ping or a pong. Answers 0; `H1_INVALID` for a frame `websocketWriteFrame` refuses, a close (that is `closeWebSocket`), or one larger than the output; `H1_AGAIN` when it does not fit yet; `H1_CLOSED` when the slot is not an open WebSocket. A window outside `buf` panics. |
| `unpark(): void` | Takes back the buffers `park` gave away, before bytes are fed. A parked buffer is `noOutput` itself, which a pointer compare finds without loading the empty array's header from a line the request touches nowhere else; any other empty buffer is still swapped for a lent one. |
| `wantsWrite(): boolean` | Whether the output holds bytes to send. |
| `write(buf: readonly u8[], off: i32, len: i32): i32` | Writes `buf[off .. off + len)` of the response body, as much as the output has room for, and answers how much: a chunk of a chunked body, or bytes of one with a length (more than it still owes is `H1_INVALID`). When not everything was taken, `H1_WRITE` says when to try the rest; `H1_AGAIN` when nothing was. A response with no body takes everything and sends nothing. `H1_CLOSED` with no response under way. A window outside `buf` panics. Once the bytes taken reach the `Content-Length`, the response is finished whether or not `end` follows; a chunked body still needs `end`. |

### Http1OutputPool

Output buffers shared by the connections of one pool, each `size` bytes. A
connection borrows one when it has something to write and gives it back
once its carrier has sent everything, so a pool's output memory follows the
connections the socket is holding back, not the slots: Go's `net/http`
pools its writers the same way, and uWebSockets shares one per loop. A
buffer is made only when none is free, so the pool grows to the most
connections ever writing at once and then allocates nothing.

```ts
class Http1OutputPool
```

| Member | |
| --- | --- |
| `new Http1OutputPool(size: i32)` | An empty pool: no buffer is made until the first `take`. |
| `free: u8[][]` | The buffers given back and not yet taken again; `made - free.length` is how many are out. |
| `made: i32` | How many buffers the pool has made. |

### Http1Server

A pool of HTTP/1.1 connections over plain TCP on one listening socket.
`slot`s are the indices `accept` answers; a slot is the program's from
`accept` until it calls `close`, and its descriptor is `fd(slot)`.

```ts
class Http1Server
```

| Member | |
| --- | --- |
| `new Http1Server(config: Http1Config, listener: i32, size: i32)` | A pool of `size` slots, at least one, serving `config` on `listener`. No slot is built here: a slot's connection and its buffers are allocated by the first `accept` into it and kept, so a pool sized for a peak costs at start-up only the read scratch, the shared `Date` and the output pool, and at most `size` connections once the peak has come. |
| `connections: Http1Connection[]` | The connections built so far, slot `k`'s at `k`: one per slot ever accepted into, and slot 0's once `connection` has asked for it. |
| `date: HttpDate` | The `Date` every slot's responses carry, formatted once a second for all of them and read from the clock once per serve call: `readable` and `writable` hold a reading and `flush` lets it go. `date.pin` fixes its clock. |
| `expireScans: i32` | How many calls of `expire` walked every slot, for a program measuring its cost. |
| `fds: i32[]` | Each slot's descriptor, or -1 while it is free, for the slots accepted into so far: its length is the high-water mark, and a slot past it has never been used. |
| `free: i32[]` | The slots closed since they were used, a stack whose top `accept` takes before it builds a slot past the high-water mark: finding one costs the same with every slot free as with all but one busy, where a scan of `fds` walked the busy ones. |
| `heads: Http1OutputPool` | The head buffers resting slots lend, beside `inputs`; `made` counts how many the slots ever needed. |
| `inputs: Http1OutputPool` | The input and head buffers resting slots lend, with `Http1Config.idleInput`. |
| `outputs: Http1OutputPool` | The output buffers the slots borrow while they write. |
| `accept(): i32` | Accepts the next waiting connection into a free slot and answers the slot, which the program adds to its loop with `H1_WANT_READ`; -11 when none is waiting, `H1_POOL_FULL` when every slot is busy (the connection is closed), or `tcpAccept`'s own failure. |
| `busy(): i32` | How many slots hold a connection. |
| `close(slot: i32): void` | Closes `slot`'s socket, whatever is left unsent, and frees the slot. |
| `connection(slot: i32): Http1Connection` | The connection of `slot`. A slot never accepted into, or out of range, names slot 0's connection, which this builds when no slot has been yet (the first `accept` then takes it, restarted). |
| `expire(now: i64): i32` | Closes every slot that has been idle past `idleTimeout`, or reading one head for longer than `headTimeout`, or lingering past `lingerTimeout`, at `now` (`monotonicNanos`); answers how many. |
| `fd(slot: i32): i32` | The descriptor of `slot`, for `pollAdd`; -1 for a free or unknown one. |
| `flush(slot: i32): i32` | Sends what `slot`'s connection holds until the socket would block, and answers the interest: `H1_DONE` once the connection is over and sent, otherwise read while it has room and write while it holds bytes or a write is held back (its `H1_WRITE` comes from `next` once the socket is writable, even when this send emptied the output). It ends the serve call, so a response written after it reads the clock anew. Once a refusal (`H1_ERROR`) is sent the slot lingers: its write side is shut and what the client still sends is drained, answering `H1_WANT_READ` until the client's end of stream, `lingerBytes`, or `expire` past `lingerTimeout`; `next` answers `H1_NEED_MORE` meanwhile. |
| `holds(slot: i32): boolean` | Whether `slot` is a slot of this pool that holds a connection. |
| `next(slot: i32): i32` | `slot`'s connection's next event; `H1_ERROR` for a free slot. While a write is held back the output is sent first, so that the room it waits for is made here and `H1_WRITE` comes in the same pass; otherwise what the program writes in answer to one event and the next goes out together at `flush`, as one segment rather than several. |
| `readable(slot: i32): i32` | The socket of `slot` is readable: reads it while the connection has room and the socket has more, then sends. Answers the interest. It begins a serve call, which the program's `flush` of the slot ends: the responses written in between carry one clock reading as their `Date`. |
| `rearm(slot: i32, wants: i32): boolean` | Whether the program must `pollModify` `slot`'s descriptor to `wants`, the interest `readable`, `writable` or `flush` answered, and records it as armed when it must. A keep-alive connection answers the same interest request after request, and each `pollModify` is a system call (`epoll_ctl`) that changes nothing. |
| `size(): i32` | How many slots the pool has, built or not. |
| `writable(slot: i32): i32` | The socket of `slot` is writable: sends, and begins a serve call as `readable` does. Answers the interest. |

### Http1TlsServer

A pool of HTTP/1.1 connections over TLS 1.3 on one listening socket: one
`Http1Connection` beside each slot of a `TlsTcpServer`, run the way
`nish/net/http2-tls` runs HTTP/2. A handshake that chose ALPN `http/1.1`,
or none (a client that does not send ALPN speaks HTTP/1.1), reaches its
connection; any other protocol is shut down with `close_notify`. A slot's
connection is built on the first accept into it and kept, as
`Http1Server`'s is.

```ts
class Http1TlsServer
```

| Member | |
| --- | --- |
| `new Http1TlsServer(tlsConfig: TlsServerConfig, config: Http1Config, listener: i32, size: i32)` | A pool of `size` slots, at least one, serving `config` over TLS under `tlsConfig` on `listener`. No slot is built here: the first `accept` into a slot builds its connection and, in `tls`, its handshake state, and keeps them, so a pool sized for a peak costs at start-up only the read scratches, the shared `Date` and the empty pools. |
| `connections: Http1Connection[]` | The connections built so far, slot `k`'s at `k`: one per slot ever accepted into. `connection` never adds to it; a slot never built reads `vacant` instead. |
| `date: HttpDate` | The `Date` every slot's responses carry, as `Http1Server.date` is. |
| `expireScans: i32` | How many calls of `expire` walked every slot. |
| `outputs: Http1OutputPool` | The output buffers the slots borrow while they write. |
| `tls: TlsTcpServer` | The TLS 1.3 pool underneath, one slot beside each connection; read it for a slot's TLS connection. |
| `accept(serverRandom: u8[], ephemeralPrivate: u8[]): i32` | Accepts the next waiting connection as `TlsTcpServer.accept` does, with the caller's 32-byte server random and x25519 key, and gives it a fresh connection, building the slot's on its first accept. Answers the slot, or what `TlsTcpServer.accept` answers. |
| `alpn(slot: i32): string` | The ALPN protocol `slot`'s handshake chose, or empty. |
| `busy(): i32` | How many slots hold a connection. |
| `close(slot: i32): void` | Ends `slot`'s connection and frees the slot at once, as `TlsTcpServer.close` does. |
| `connection(slot: i32): Http1Connection` | The HTTP/1.1 connection of `slot`. A slot never accepted into answers `vacant`, as a free slot answers a connection that holds nothing, and builds no slot; a slot out of range names slot 0's. |
| `expire(now: i64): i32` | Closes every slot that has been idle past `idleTimeout`, or reading one head for longer than `headTimeout`, at `now` (`monotonicNanos`); answers how many. |
| `fd(slot: i32): i32` | The descriptor of `slot`, for `pollAdd`; -1 for a free one. |
| `flush(slot: i32): i32` | Writes what `slot`'s connection holds into TLS, as far as TLS takes it, and sends it; shuts TLS down once the connection is over or ALPN chose another protocol. Answers TLS's interest, with the write bit while the connection still holds bytes or a write is held back. |
| `holds(slot: i32): boolean` | Whether `slot` holds a connection. |
| `next(slot: i32): i32` | Moves what TLS has decrypted for `slot` into its connection, as far as the connection has room, and answers the connection's next event. A free slot, or one whose ALPN was another protocol, answers `H1_ERROR`. |
| `readable(slot: i32): i32` | The socket of `slot` is readable: TLS reads it, and what the connection has to send goes after. Answers the interest. |
| `refused(slot: i32): boolean` | Whether `slot`'s handshake is done and chose a protocol other than `http/1.1`. |
| `signP256(slot: i32, key: Secret<u8[]>): i32` | Signs `slot`'s CertificateVerify with `key`, as `TlsTcpServer.signP256` does. Answers the interest. |
| `size(): i32` | How many slots the pool has, built or not. |
| `writable(slot: i32): i32` | The socket of `slot` is writable. Answers the interest. |

### HttpDate

The `Date` field an origin server with a clock sends on every final
response (RFC 9110 §6.6.1): the IMF-fixdate of now, in 29 bytes the object
owns and rewrites in place, at most once a second.

It reads the wall clock, `Date.now()`, which a wasm32 build has no host for,
so it lives here, in a module that is native already, while the formatting
it calls, `httpDateWrite`, stays in `nish/net/http-fields`, which compiles
for wasm32 (the split `nish/crypto/x509` and `x509-random` make). `pin`
replaces the clock with one instant, which is how a test asserts a response
byte for byte. `hold` reads the clock once for a run of responses, a serve
call's, until `unhold`; `pin` wins over it.

```ts
class HttpDate
```

| Member | |
| --- | --- |
| `new HttpDate()` | A date on the wall clock, with nothing formatted yet. |
| `clockReads(): i64` | How many times the wall clock has been read: once per `hold`, and once per `current` outside one. |
| `current(): u8[]` | The 29 bytes for now, which are rewritten only when the second differs from the one they hold — earlier as well as later, since a corrected clock steps back. It allocates nothing, and the array is the same one each time, so a caller copies it out rather than keeping it. A wall clock before 1970 or past 9999 answers the nearer of the two ends. |
| `formats(): i64` | How many times the bytes have been rewritten: one per second that `current` was asked for, at most. |
| `hold(): void` | Reads the wall clock once and makes `current` answer that reading until `unhold`, so the responses of one serve call cost one read. A pinned date reads nothing. A second `hold` takes a fresh reading. |
| `pin(unixMs: i64): boolean` | Makes `current` answer `unixMs`, milliseconds since 1970, until `unpin`. False, and nothing changed, for an instant before 1970-01-01T00:00:00Z or after 9999-12-31T23:59:59.999Z, which an IMF-fixdate cannot name. |
| `unhold(): void` | Puts `current` back on a clock read per call, for a response written outside a serve call. |
| `unpin(): void` | Puts `current` back on the wall clock. |

## Constants

<scalar-grid cols="2">

<scalar-card title="-11" icon="phosphor/regular/hash">

`H1_AGAIN: i32`

Nothing fits yet: Linux's EAGAIN, as `nish:net` spells it.

</scalar-card>

<scalar-card title="&quot;http/1.1&quot;" icon="phosphor/regular/hash">

`H1_ALPN: string`

The ALPN protocol identifier of HTTP/1.1 (RFC 7301 §6).

</scalar-card>

<scalar-card title="2" icon="phosphor/regular/hash">

`H1_BODY: i32`

Request body bytes: `data[dataStart .. dataStart + dataLength)`, valid until the next `next()`.

</scalar-card>

<scalar-card title="-32" icon="phosphor/regular/hash">

`H1_CLOSED: i32`

No exchange the call belongs to: Linux's EPIPE.

</scalar-card>

<scalar-card title="16" icon="phosphor/regular/hash">

`H1_DONE: i32`

The slot's connection is over and every byte is sent: `close` it.

</scalar-card>

<scalar-card title="3" icon="phosphor/regular/hash">

`H1_END: i32`

The request is complete.

</scalar-card>

<scalar-card title="7" icon="phosphor/regular/hash">

`H1_ERROR: i32`

The input broke a rule; `status` is the HTTP status or WebSocket close code sent. Final.

</scalar-card>

<scalar-card title="-22" icon="phosphor/regular/hash">

`H1_INVALID: i32`

Something the server may not send: Linux's EINVAL.

</scalar-card>

<scalar-card title="0" icon="phosphor/regular/hash">

`H1_NEED_MORE: i32`

`next`: nothing to hand over until more input arrives, the output drains, or the program answers.

</scalar-card>

<scalar-card title="-105" icon="phosphor/regular/hash">

`H1_POOL_FULL: i32`

`accept`: every slot was busy, so the connection was accepted and closed. Linux's ENOBUFS.

</scalar-card>

<scalar-card title="1" icon="phosphor/regular/hash">

`H1_REQUEST: i32`

A request's head was read: `parser` holds it.

</scalar-card>

<scalar-card title="1" icon="phosphor/regular/hash">

`H1_WANT_READ: i32`

Interest bits, the same as `nish/net/tls/record-server`'s: the low two are `pollModify`'s events.

</scalar-card>

<scalar-card title="2" icon="phosphor/regular/hash">

`H1_WANT_WRITE: i32`

The slot has output waiting for the socket: ask the readiness loop for writable.

</scalar-card>

<scalar-card title="4" icon="phosphor/regular/hash">

`H1_WRITE: i32`

A `write`, `respond`, `end` or `sendFrame` that answered `H1_AGAIN` may be tried again.

</scalar-card>

<scalar-card title="6" icon="phosphor/regular/hash">

`H1_WS_CLOSE: i32`

The WebSocket peer closed with `status` (1005 for none); the close is answered. Final.

</scalar-card>

<scalar-card title="5" icon="phosphor/regular/hash">

`H1_WS_MESSAGE: i32`

A WebSocket message: `opcode`, `data[dataStart .. dataStart + dataLength)`.

</scalar-card>

</scalar-grid>
